refrigerantsAndFluoro.fact: China 2026 HFC production quota 797,800 t; Juhua 299,900 t (37.58%); top-6 hold ~90%; 2027 draft keeps 2026 framework; China controlled use to fall to 90% of baseline by 1-Jan-2029.

China R32 ~CNY63,000/t (Dec-2025) and CNY62,700-65,500/t (Jun-2026, decade high, +19% to +77% YoY depending on series); R134a CNY62,500-65,000/t (Jun-2026); R125 CNY46,000/t and R22 CNY16,000/t (Dec-2025).
China R32 exports Jan-Apr 2026 7,032 t (-50% YoY); AHF prices +~40% YTD 2026; sulphur +210% YTD.
India domestic R32 demand ~17,000-18,000 t vs larger installed capacity, so Indian producers export; Indian AC industry expected to grow robustly in FY27.

Kigali / AIM Act / F-gas phase-downs (see company.json refrigerants.quotaRegimes): India freeze 2028 on 2024-26 baseline; US allowances 60% of baseline 2024-28 then 30% 2029-33; EU HFC consumption phase-out by 2050.

Competitors: Navin Fluorine (mcap ~Rs43,600cr, FY26 sales Rs3,314cr, 33% OPM), Gujarat Fluorochemicals (mcap ~Rs46,800cr, FY26 sales Rs4,996cr, 24% OPM), Tanfac (small); global: Chemours (also SRF partner), Honeywell, Daikin, Chinese Juhua/Dongyue. Global market size not sourced.

specialtyChemicals.fact: FY26: elevated inventories, Chinese pricing pressure and sluggish agrochem demand; innovators slowed launches/registrations under generic pressure. Early 2026: China pricing bottoming, agro volumes recovering in pockets; innovators de-risking supply chains from Europe/China towards India.

packagingFilms.fact: India flexible packaging film cycle: BOPET capacity +~45% and BOPP +~20% over FY22-23 vs domestic demand +~11%; industry profitability hit a decadal low (~8%).

FY27 outlook (SRF): film demand healthy but new BOPP capacity in India may pressure margins; BOPET better balanced; China anti-involution measures lifted BOPET prices in Q4FY26; GST 2.0 repack hit demand in Q3FY26.

Peers: Cosmo First (FY26 sales Rs3,639cr, OPM 11%), Polyplex (Rs7,086cr, 4.9%), Uflex (Rs15,401cr, 12%), Jindal Poly Films (Rs2,899cr, negative OPM). Polyplex adding 52,400 tpa BOPET in India (H1 FY28).
Battery foil: India >150 GWh Li-ion cell capacity committed/expected by 2030; ACC PLI Rs18,100cr outlay, 40 GWh awarded, 58 GWh waitlisted.

technicalTextiles.fact: SRF #1 in India for tyre cord fabrics (60,000 tpa) and 22,000 tpa belting; FY26 pressures from low-cost imports, lactam volatility, US reciprocal tariffs on belting and PIY QCO withdrawal; QCO stay order from May-2026 helped PIY; US tariff rationalisation revived belting exports.

chinaPlusOne.fact: Global innovators de-risking supply chains away from Europe and China toward India (management, Oct-2026); but Chinese overcapacity has kept specialty pricing under pressure since FY24.

moat.evidence: 539 patents filed, 160 granted; 500+ R&D/scale-up staff, 50+ products in pipeline; in-house non-infringing HFO process described as a global benchmark on capex and opex; CTG moved 35+ molecules to scale-up in FY26.

Chemours chose SRF to build FEP/FKM plants on an ROI-style contract; 7-8 agro AIs in advanced stage with innovators; two Western pharma innovators incl. an oncology molecule; long-term FMCG film contracts (Nestle, PepsiCo R&D collaborations).

moat.dimension: Cost position vs China - specialty chemicals
moat.evidence: Chinese overcapacity forced price cuts (DFPA at "unsustainably low levels"); specialty revenue -6.7% in FY26 and margin squeeze in Q2FY27; SRF chose to defend share rather than price. Some products are exported into China, showing cost competitiveness in select molecules.
Backward-integrated HF/AHF and resin; new 30,000 tpa HF at Odisha; but China quota-holders (Juhua 37.6% of China quota) set global prices and AHF costs rose ~40% in 2026.

India quotas from 2028 based on 2024-26 production; SRF has run HFC plants flat-out through the baseline and is debottlenecking to >65,000 tpa; new entrants without 2024-26 production get no quota post-2027 (company view).

Leading global HFC/HFC-blend player; sole Indian producer of some refrigerants (Crisil); #1 Indian tyre cord maker (60,000 tpa); 16 plants in 4 countries; post-HFO expects top 3-4 global refrigerant maker.

Commodity BOPET/BOPP with repeated oversupply (industry capacity BOPET +45%/BOPP +20% vs demand +11% over FY22-23); SRF film EBIT margin 4.6-9.9% FY24-26 outside the war-driven Q1FY27 spike; moving to value-added (capacitor film, BOPA, thick film, foil).
Crisil AA+/Stable; net debt/EBITDA 1.02x and net debt/equity 0.27x (FY26); interest cover 12.65x; accruals >Rs2,500cr/yr fund ~Rs2,500cr capex.
Ran film plants flat-out through the 2026 Middle East disruption while competitors shut, winning new customers; DTA unit + global sourcing.

critiques.point: Refrigerant prices are near a cyclical peak; the HFC-to-HFO and supply-tightness tailwinds are already priced in - mean reversion risk.

Specialty chemicals (largest chemicals sub-business pre-FY26) faces structural Chinese overcapacity; the entire Q2FY27 chemicals margin decline came from specialty; earnings acceleration may wait till FY29 and valuations still look full.
Specialty challenges could persist longer than anticipated - chemicals multiple should be cut to 20x from 25x; the Street is not convinced of the promised H2 recovery.
Subdued agrochemical demand and persistent Chinese oversupply keep the stock a Hold even after the correction.
AI/new-molecule commercialisation keeps slipping (talked about for ~3 years); depends on innovators' registrations - timing uncertain "to say it mildly".
critiques.who: ICICI Securities analyst question; management answer (Jul-2026)

critiques.point: Valuation stretched historically (47x forward P/E, >2 SD above average in Feb-2025) with EPS estimates 16-17% below consensus.
Downside risk to consensus from Chinese pricing pressure and delays in key product commercialisation; margin sustainability doubtful.
Q1FY27 record was a one-off (war-driven film supply shortage, panic buying, inventory gains); Q2 films margin fell back to 9.7%.
Heavy, long-gestation capex (~Rs2,500cr/yr; HFO only from Q4FY28, fluoropolymers full-stream FY29) while asset turnover is ~0.65x and ROE ~14%; depreciation and interest precede revenue.
critiques.who: GAM synthesis of company data; Kotak (growth waits till FY29)

critiques.point: Hedging policy has cost money: forex (ECF) losses Rs188cr in FY26 and ~Rs165cr in H1FY27 from long-dated export covers.
Post-baseline competition: CY2027 is a "free year" and many R32 capacity announcements exist; India HCFC treatment in quota unresolved until early 2027.
Promoter KAMA Holdings sought approval to sell up to 3% (could go below 50%) - so far only an inter-se transfer, but a potential overhang.
Freight inflation of 15-20%+ on some routes cannot be fully passed through in price-sensitive markets; working capital lengthening with crude.
